on-demand on a dynamic web server.
So instead of just having a single HTML file
and letting client-side Angular do everything,
with a server-side rendered app,
when a user wants to visit a certain page,
the request is handled on the server first,
and the page that was requested is pre-rendered on-demand
on the server
so that the finished page is sent back to the user.

and having client-side JavaScript do everything,
the user receives the finished page with all its content.

that page still includes lots of Angular JavaScript code,
which then takes over
and hydrates the page once it has been received
by the browser.

so that you get the best of both worlds,
instant responses due to client-side JavaScript
doing the heavy work,
but at the same time,
finished pages without missing content
for the initial request.
Now, when going for a server-side rendered app,
you therefore need a dynamic web server
which is able to run code on it

A server that's just able to return HTML

Instead, it must be a server

because it's that compiled JavaScript code,
your Angular code compiled to JavaScript,

Now, the advantage of building

In addition, we have increased complexity

and we must set up this application
to support server-side rendering.
